questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has its right angle at C. Explain why sin A = cos B.
questions.prompt_markup: Right triangle ABC has its right angle at C. Explain why sin A = cos B.
questions.correct_answer: sin A = BC/AB = cos B, and A and B are complementary.
questions.required_method: Name the side opposite ∠A and the side adjacent to ∠B, and use the angle sum.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: sin A = BC/AB (opposite over hypotenuse); cos B = BC/AB (BC is adjacent to ∠B); so they are equal; ∠A + ∠B = 90°, so sin A = cos(90° - A).
